sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the matzah eaten after the Giving of the Torah is superior even to the matzah of the first Passover, because its revelation comes through prior service in Torah and mitzvos, analogous to the superiority of the revelation at Shavuos over that of the Exodus.

translations.translation: And it can be said that the matzah that we eat after the Giving of the Torah
is on a higher level even than the aspect of the matzah of the first Passover before the Giving of the Torah.

For since the revelation of the King of Kings, the Holy One Blessed be He, in the matzah that we eat after the Giving of the Torah comes through the precedence of service in the fulfillment of Torah and mitzvos throughout the entire year
(before Passover),
it is a more elevated revelation.

And this is analogous to the superiority of the revelation of the Festival of Shavuos, the time of the Giving of the Torah, after the service of the Counting of the Omer, over the revelation of the Exodus from Egypt,
for the revelation of the Exodus from Egypt,
although it was an exceedingly lofty revelation
(in His very glory and essence),
nevertheless,
since the revelation was from Above,
it was only temporary,
and through the service of the Counting of the Omer,
the service of the lower being
(after the revelation of the Exodus),
they draw down, in addition to the forty-nine gates,
after the completion of the forty-nine gates,
also the fiftieth gate
(and this gate too is drawn down through our service, as it is said,
"You shall count fifty days"),
and within the fiftieth gate itself—in addition to its lower aspect, which is related to the forty-nine gates
(analogous to Arich),
also its higher aspect
which is above any relation to the forty-nine gates
(analogous to Atik),
which is more elevated
even than the revelation of the Exodus from Egypt.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section adds that the matzah we eat after the Giving of the Torah is superior also because the eating of the matzah itself is a mitzvah, unlike the matzah at the first Passover which was primarily due to the dough not having time to leaven.

translations.translation: And it can be added that the superiority of the matzah we eat after the Giving of the Torah over the matzah after midnight that existed then
is
(in addition to the fact that the revelation in the matzah we eat comes through the precedence of service in the fulfillment of Torah and mitzvos before Passover,
but rather)
also because the eating of the matzah itself is a mitzvah.
For the matzah after midnight at that time was
(primarily)
because the dough of our forefathers did not have time to become leavened
(due to the revelation from Above),
and there was no service in this
(or fulfillment of a mitzvah).
But the matzah we eat after the Giving of the Torah is connected with the service of man,
the fulfillment of the mitzvah of eating matzah.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section resolves the apparent contradiction by explaining that the Haggadah's statement about the matzah refers to the inclusion of the original aspect of "not having time to leaven" within the matzah we eat, which also contains the higher levels of post-Torah service and even the aspect of future redemption.

translations.translation: And it must be understood: When we say, "This matzah that we eat, for what reason? Because the dough of our forefathers did not have time to become leavened,"
behold, the matzah that we eat
(after the Giving of the Torah)
has the superiority of service and the virtue of fulfilling a mitzvah
[and within this itself—a mitzvah after the Giving of the Torah],
so how can we say that the matzah we eat is because it did not have time to become leavened
(for that it is matzah and not chametz came about by itself,
because it did not have time to become leavened)?
And the explanation can be given as follows:
For the mitzvah of telling the story of the Exodus from Egypt is to relate the matter of the Exodus as it was then.
And furthermore
(and primarily),
since had the Holy One Blessed be He not taken our forefathers out of Egypt, etc., we would still be enslaved to Pharaoh in Egypt,
therefore even now
(and especially on Passover night),
even though we are already after the Exodus and after the Giving of the Torah,
the state and condition that existed then also exists.
Therefore we say
(in the telling of the Exodus in the Haggadah)

"This matzah that we eat... for what reason? Because the dough of our forefathers did not have time to become leavened until the King of Kings, the Holy One Blessed be He, revealed Himself to them and redeemed them,"

for in the matzah that we eat before midnight, there is, in addition to the virtue of the matzah before midnight—the virtue of the service of the lower being in fulfilling the command of the Holy One Blessed be He
(as it was before the Giving of the Torah),
also the virtue of the matzah after midnight—the virtue of "it did not have time to become leavened"
(in which leavening is impossible)
due to the revelation from Above.
And in addition to this,
in the matzah that we eat there is also the elevation from the aspect of the Giving of the Torah,
the fulfillment of a mitzvah after the Giving of the Torah.
And furthermore,
it also contains something of the virtue of eating matzah on the seventh day of Passover, which is optional
(above obligation),
which is akin to the eating of the future to come.
